stem: With ZNE enabled as shown, what is `raw.shape`?
code:
# qc has ONE parameter; estimator is a Runtime EstimatorV2 on a QPU
estimator.options.resilience.zne_mitigation = True
estimator.options.resilience.zne.noise_factors = (1, 3, 5, 7)

observables = [[obs_a], [obs_b]]
values = [[0.1], [0.2], [0.3]]
result = estimator.run([(isa_qc, observables, values)]).result()
raw = result[0].data.evs_noise_factors

explanation.correct: First the PUB shape: `[[obs_a], [obs_b]]` is (2, 1), and three one-element rows on a one-parameter circuit are 3 parameter sets of shape (3,), so the PUB broadcasts to (2, 3). With ZNE on, `evs_noise_factors` keeps the raw estimate at every noise factor, documented as shape `(*shape, num_noise_factors)`: four factors append a trailing axis of 4, giving (2, 3, 4). `evs` itself stays (2, 3), holding the extrapolated values.

distractors.A: That is the shape of `evs`, which holds the extrapolated zero-noise estimates. The per-factor raw values need an extra axis.
distractors.B: Puts the noise-factor axis first. The ZNE fields append their extra axes after the PUB shape, so each PUB element's values over the noise factors sit along the last axis.
distractors.D: Counts the zero-noise evaluation point too. `[0, *noise_factors]` is the default for `extrapolated_noise_factors`, which shapes `evs_extrapolated`, not the raw `evs_noise_factors`.
distractors.E: Flattens the PUB into 6 elements. Result arrays keep the broadcast shape (2, 3) rather than a single flat axis.

provenance.notes: R2 add (d3, conceptual): PUB broadcasting with one-parameter coercion ((2,1) x 3 sets -> (2,3)) combined with the ZNE result field shape (*shape, num_noise_factors). ZNE data fields exist only on the server; shape rule quoted from the ZneOptions docstring (identical in installed 0.48.0 source and the live API page, fetched 2026-10-01).
